transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-12 14:00 PT | Duration: ~75 minutes | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Olivia (Redwood CSM), Marta (Trident Head Infra), Liam (Trident SecArch), Rashid (Trident Cloud Eng), Nia (Trident Compliance)

Summary: Deep technical walkthrough of private/VPC/on-prem security architecture for Redwood Private. Focus: network isolation patterns, ingress/egress gating, host-level hardening, RBAC/SSO integration, KMS/encryption model, and audit log provenance for SOC 2/ISO evidence. Customer wants a pilot that demonstrates zero-trust perimeter and clear proof of auditability for PHI workloads.

Topics covered: network zoning, egress proxy options, sidecar vs host-proxy, VPC endpoints, NAT vs egress proxies, firewall stateful rules vs cloud NACLs, host hardening (CIS, eBPF), KV cache encryption and KMS rotation, audit log chaining and retention, SSO/SAML mapping to RBAC, data residency constraints.

[00:00] Samira: "All right, thanks everyone for joining, we'll run about an hour, hour and 15, try to leave time for Q&A. Quick intros?"
[00:18] Marta: "I'm Marta, I run infra at Trident, we've got a lot of sensitive patient PII so SOC 2 and ISO are musts for any private deployment."
[00:26] Liam: "Security architect here, focused on network and auth, mostly concerned with egress controls and key management."
[00:33] Diego: "Diego from Redwood SE, I usually dig into network patterns and host isolation, happy to run the deep bits today."
[01:05] Samira: "High level: Trident intends to run Redwood Private in their VPC with an optional on-prem edge for air-gapped sites, right?"
[01:12] Marta: "Yes — majority in AWS accounts, small on-prem footprint for legacy PACS imaging stores."
[01:28] Liam: "Key constraints: no outbound to uncontrolled internet from model hosts, all egress must be through approved proxies with TLS inspection at our egress point. Also strict key custody - we need KMS backed by our HSM. And audit logs must be immutable and sent to our SIEM with signed provenance."
[01:52] Diego: "Understood. Two main patterns we recommend: 1) VPC-isolated deployment with egress through a managed egress proxy (HTTP/TCP proxy behind a NAT and explicit allow-lists), or 2) host-side sidecar proxies that enforce per-container egress rules and mTLS to outbound services. Both can be used together."
[02:10] Liam: "Sidecar is interesting, but we worry about operational complexity across mixed on-prem and cloud."
[02:25] Diego: "Yeah, for hybrid we often use a lightweight host proxy plus central egress gateway. For on-prem you can run an on-prem egress gateway appliance (or container) that terminates egress, does TLS origination to approved upstreams, and provides ACLs. We can also enforce DNS pinning to prevent bypass."
[03:00] Rashid (overlap, slight crosstalk): "Question, how do you handle KV cache? We can't have secrets in plaintext on the host, and the performance hit for encrypt/decrypt every token might be bad."
[03:18] Diego: "Good call. Redwood's runtime supports local encrypted KV cache with envelope encryption: model keys are encrypted with customer KMS (you control the CMKs) and the runtime caches an unwrapped ephemeral key in memory only. No persistent unencrypted tokens on disk. In on-prem, we integrate with your HSM/KMS via mTLS and PKCS#11 if required. The tradeoff is KMS calls on cache cold-starts; we recommend a short-lived wrapping key with client-side caching to reduce roundtrips."
[03:52] Nia: "For audit, we need end-to-end logs showing who requested which model with which dataset, timestamps, and proof of non-repudiation for each change. Do you sign logs?"
[04:06] Olivia: "We provide audit events from the control plane and from the runtime. For private deployments the runtime can forward signed audit bundles to your log collector. We can also support write-once object store retention for logs and a signed Merkle-tree style proof of log integrity if you need chain-of-custody evidence."
[04:34] Marta: "That's encouraging. For SOC 2 we also need RBAC and SSO integration. How granular is the RBAC?"
[04:46] Diego: "We map SAML attributes from your IdP into RBAC roles. Roles can be as granular as per-model and per-route. You can restrict who can start inference on 'clinical-model-v2' vs 'general-model', and also restrict export of embeddings. All actions are logged with the user principal."
[05:15] Liam: "What about control plane connectivity? We want the control plane in a private link to our VPC; we can't have an open control plane talking to every host over internet."
[05:26] Samira: "For Redwood Private we offer a private control-plane connector: a small agent in your VPC establishes an outbound-only mTLS connection to our control endpoints over a single egress IP, or you can host the control plane entirely in your environment for air-gapped. There's an option to use AWS PrivateLink or customer-managed reverse proxy."
[05:51] Rashid: "Outbound-only is good. But can we pin ports and do deep packet inspection on the egress?"
[06:02] Diego: "The connector uses TLS over 443 by default but can be configured to a different port. For DPI, you get standard SNI and certs; if you need payload inspection we support mutual TLS to a proxy so your proxy can terminate and inspect before forwarding to Redwood. For egress allow-lists we provide a short list of FQDNs and IP ranges; if you prefer domain allow-lists via proxy, that's fine."
[06:30] Liam: "Tell us more about firewalling and NACL interplay. Our infra team favors NACLs for stateless control but also layer 7 rules."
[06:42] Diego: "Best practice: use security groups for host-level stateful rules and NACLs as a coarse-grained boundary. For L7, run a sidecar or host-proxy that can enforce domain names and HTTP methods. We also recommend using eBPF/XDP to prevent bypass of host proxies if you have that capability."
[07:08] Marta: "Can we do network zoning where model hosts cannot reach internet except the egress gateway, and only the egress gateway can reach external model registries?"
[07:20] Diego: "Absolutely. We call that an airlock pattern: model hosts in private subnets with no default route, route 0.0.0.0/0 is via the egress gateway, and the egress gateway has strict allow lists. For on-prem we mirror with VLANs and host ACLs."
[07:45] Nia: "Retention for logs — SOC 2 evidence needs at least 1 year of logs, and ISO may ask for more. Are logs exportable to our S3 bucket with server-side encryption using our CMK?"
[07:58] Olivia: "Yes, logs can be pushed to your S3 with SSE-KMS using your CMK. For chain-of-custody we can sign bundles before export. We also support streaming to your SIEM via syslog over TLS or an SQS/SNS ingestion pattern."
[08:25] Liam: "About data residency — some PHI must remain in specific regions, can we restrict model hosting to a region and deny failover to other regions?"
[08:36] Samira: "You can pin workloads to region-specific pools and explicit fallback policies. If a host fails we won't failover to another region unless you allow it. That's configured at the route level."
[08:53] Rashid: "KMS rotation cadence — we have monthly rotation rules. How does your runtime cope with rotated keys?"
[09:03] Diego: "We support key-rotation-friendly envelope encryption: old wrapped keys remain decryptable until you revoke them; runtime can retrieve new wrapped keys transparently. For strict rotation you can force a full cache rewrap; it's a short maintenance window. We can simulate the rotation in the pilot to show impact."
[09:27] Marta: "We also require proof that no admin can read raw model inference logs. Who has root?"
[09:36] Olivia: "In Private on your VPC the control plane admin accounts are under your SSO and RBAC. Redwood employees cannot access runtime data unless you grant a support session with explicit audit and egress to your log store. Support access is logged and you can require session approvals."
[09:58] Liam: "Can you run an offline scan showing attack surface on an example subnet?"
[10:07] Diego: "Yes, we can produce a report: expected open ports, required ports (eg, 443 for control, 22 only if you enable SSH bastion), sidecar ports, egress lists. We'll include suggested iptables/eBPF rules. I'll produce the draft."
[10:33] Marta: "On the network diagram, do you support VPC endpoints for S3 so logs never traverse internet?"
[10:40] Samira: "Yes, recommended. We can push logs to S3 via VPC Endpoint and avoid NAT egress for log upload."
[10:52] Rashid: "One nuance: our imaging centers have NATs with hairpinning issues. Will this break the connector?"
[11:02] Diego: "We have a connector that can operate over a single outbound IP and handle hairpin; if you have symmetric NAT, we recommend a small local relay that maintains the connection. We'll detail that pattern in the diagram."
[11:25] Nia: "From an audit perspective we need to show separation of duties: who can add a model, who can change routing, and who can rotate keys. How are those controls surfaced?"
[11:36] Olivia: "RBAC roles map to specific actions: model-upload, rollout, routing-change, key-management. Those map to SAML groups and we log the exact principal for each action. We can export a role mapping CSV for auditors."
[12:00] Marta: "Edge case: what if an engineer tries to bypass the sidecar and curl out?"
[12:06] Diego: "If you deploy eBPF rules we can drop packets that don't originate from the approved process or network namespace. Combined with IPTables and namespace isolation, bypass is very hard. We'll give sample eBPF policy in the repo."
[12:36] Liam: "For the pilot we want: 1) private-deploy in dev VPC, 2) on-prem connector at imaging site, 3) demo of KMS integration and log export, 4) a simple load test to show KV cache warm vs cold. Can you scope that?"
[12:52] Samira: "Yes, scope looks like a 3-week pilot: week 1 deploy & network setup, week 2 KMS wiring and log piping, week 3 bench tests and SOC2 evidence collection. Estimated cost and timelines we'll send in follow-up."
[13:12] Rashid: "About cost, any additional licensing for private control plane?"
[13:18] Samira: "Private has a platform fee plus reserved host costs; we'll include options: fully-managed control plane vs customer-hosted control plane. We'll outline security tradeoffs for both."
[13:34] Marta: "We need a written runbook for incident response: if a host is suspected compromised, how do we revoke keys and isolate traffic?"
[13:46] Diego: "Runbook is straightforward: 1) revoke the CMK or rotate the key (controls access to new unwrapping), 2) blackhole host in routing, 3) revoke SSO session tokens, 4) collect forensic logs from immutable store. We'll draft a runbook tailored to your infra."
[14:10] Nia: "One final policy ask: can we require that model outputs containing PHI never leave region or be logged outside our controlled buckets?"
[14:22] Olivia: "Yes — we can enforce redaction rules and route sensitive outputs to region-locked buckets. You can opt to never persist raw outputs outside your S3, and Redwood's runtime can be configured to redact certain fields before emitting logs."
[14:45] (Longer segment of clarifying questions about tooling and shared artifacts)
[20:12] Diego: "I'll mention two technical footnotes: 1) if you run GPU hosts in on-prem, driver compatibility matters for our optimized kernels; we'll provide a recommended driver list. 2) quantized models change memory access patterns so we advise monitoring host OOM and KV cache eviction thresholds."
[20:40] Rashid: "Driver list and a checklist for procurement would be very helpful."
[21:00] Samira: "Action items recap: Diego will share eBPF/iptables patterns and sidecar guide; Samira will send SOC2 snapshot and private-deploy reference diagram; Liam/Rashid to share VPC map; then schedule pilot kickoff. Any blockers?"
[21:18] Marta: "No blockers, just need the documents and we'll get security approval asap."
[21:28] Olivia: "We'll also share a template auditor packet showing the logs and role mappings auditors typically ask for."
[21:40] (Wrap up, exchanges of calendar invites and links)
[22:10] Samira: "Thanks all — we will follow up with the diagram, runbook, and pilot scope. Expect first artefacts by Friday."

Notes/Links referenced during call: private-deploy reference diagram (link: https://redwood.example/internal/private-deploy-reference.pdf), SOC2 snapshot (link: https://redwood.example/security/soc2-summary.pdf), sidecar pattern repo (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar-patterns - note: internal draft).

Closing recap (verbatim):
Samira: "Next steps — we'll send the network diagram and runbook, Diego will give the eBPF and iptables samples, Trident will provide VPC map, then pilot kickoff. Thanks everyone."

End of transcript.
